positions.thesis: AUDNZD at 1.2456 is a five-year extreme while NZDUSD still sits in the cheap tail at 0.5627. That cross has stretched far beyond a 30-basis-point Australia versus New Zealand 10-year gap, and it is the only concentrated, asymmetric swing on a firm tape. Short the cross as a real swing; oil remaining bid is the accepted tax, not a reason to stay flat. CORRA March stays closed: 2.55 cash versus 2.925 is the same leftover path already booked into the event-implied print, not a new dislocation…

pms.thesis: Australian-kiwi is still the five-year extreme at 1.2453, a 2.75 z-score and the 99th percentile, and the short from 1.2456 has not mean-reverted. The book stays concentrated in that fade. A one-percent squeeze on 300 million is about three million dollars against a ten million risk-capital limit, so the line is already large and is not pyramided. December and March SOFR already price hikes off 3.94 cash, which is a contested strip and not a second swing.

A US front-end receive would stack the same duration, and a US front-end pay would fight a thin premium over 3.94 cash.
